items.checks: Read both full mathematical modules and all case materials. Lifts is the original universal profinite diagram property. Discrete choice is continuous only because the source is discrete; coproduct lifts are glued on actual branches. Finite-coproduct compactness, Hausdorffness and total disconnectedness are separately supplied, so no infinite discrete compactness is claimed and empty cases remain included.

The retraction proof uses the correct composition f∘r then g∘i. Product lifts use actual open fibers of the discrete factor and prove continuity there. Finite-factor profiniteness is separate from the stronger discrete-factor lifting statement; the empty factor is covered.

Actual Ultrafilter Stone spaces and pinned continuous extensions are used. The counit is the extension of the identity on the original underlying set, is continuous and surjective, and projectivity supplies its actual continuous section. Conversely that section gives lifting against arbitrary target universes. Dense principal points prove equality after extension; no arbitrary set section is assumed continuous.

The factors are actual Ultrafilter Nat spaces satisfying the full lifting property. The concrete closed two-sheeted cover is profinite, continuous and surjective. Its hypothetical section forces the nonopen diagonal to be an open Bool fiber. This refutes the exact lifting target, beyond merely asserting lack of extremal disconnectedness.

The set-theoretic choices are made on the actual finite Hausdorff image, whose inherited topology is discrete. Their composition with the original range factorization is proved continuous, without any projectivity assumption on P. The empty-range case is included.

Actual source and target subspace fibers are indexed by range f. Restriction and gluing preserve all continuous maps and have both inverse identities; glued continuity uses the actual finite open cover. The finite-target specialization constructs and inverts genuine labelled clopen partitions, including empty blocks, and never restricts arbitrary lifts to fiberwise constant choices.
